text: Molecules with calculated LogP above the training median (3.30) have higher logD7.4.
Molecules containing a carboxylic acid have lower logD7.4 (ionised at pH 7.4).
Molecules with two or more hydrogen-bond donors have lower logD7.4.
Molecules containing a basic aliphatic amine have lower logD7.4 (protonated at pH 7.4).

Molecules containing a carboxylic acid group have lower logD7.4 than structurally similar molecules without it, because the carboxylate anion dominates at pH 7.4 (pKa ~4.5) and creates a charged species whose aqueous affinity is not captured by neutral-form MolLogP.

Molecules with zero hydrogen bond donors have higher logD7.4 than molecules possessing at least one NH or OH, because the complete absence of H-bond donation eliminates a major aqueous solvation pathway at pH 7.4.

Molecules with more than two hydrogen bond donors have lower logD7.4 than molecules with two or fewer, because multiple NH/OH groups increase aqueous solvation beyond what calculated lipophilicity alone accounts for.
Molecules with TPSA above 110 Å² have lower logD7.4 than molecules with lower TPSA, reflecting polarity-driven aqueous partitioning that persists independently of MolLogP.

Molecules containing a guanidine or amidine motif (NH2 attached to an sp2 C=N carbon) have lower logD7.4 than analogs lacking it, because the conjugate acid pKa exceeds 8 and the cationic form dominates at pH 7.4, creating ionization-driven hydrophilicity invisible to neutral-form MolLogP.

Molecules containing a primary aliphatic amine (NH2 on sp3 carbon, not adjacent to a carbonyl or aromatic ring) have lower logD7.4 than analogs lacking this group, because aliphatic primary amines are predominantly protonated at pH 7.4 (pKa ~9–10) and the resulting cation is far more hydrophilic than neutral-form MolLogP predicts.

Molecules bearing a secondary sulfonamide NH group have lower logD7.4 than N-alkyl sulfonamide analogs of comparable logP, because the sulfonamide NH donates strong H-bonds to water that the N-methyl version cannot.
